note: Clean pass (validate_items.R --table-sets: item set 3/3, resp set 1-5, PASS), 15 rows shipped, with one substantive caveat and two routine ones. (1) STEP 3b INSTRUMENT MISMATCH -- THE TABLE NAME IS MISLEADING AND SHOULD BE CORRECTED. The paper's Measures section says "Surface acting and deep acting scale were measured each with three items developed by Brotheridge and Lee(2002)" and gives the sample surface-acting item "Pretend to have emotions that I don't really have". The live sa1-sa3 items are NOT those items and are not about emotional display at all: they are S1 File questionnaire items 22-24, a three-item value-suppression block ("I suppress my own values when they differ from those of the organization", "My behavior reflects the organization's values, even if they are inconsistent with my personal beliefs", "I say things at work that I do not actually believe"). No Brotheridge & Lee wording appears anywhere in the 51 S1 headers, and the paper reproduces only that one sample item, so the study's actual surface-acting scale is not recoverable from the deposit. Two further checks agree that items 22-24 are not the analysed surface-acting block: the paper reports alpha=0.882 for surface acting, while columns 22-24 give alpha=0.690 on the 396 deposited rows (none of the deposit's block alphas reproduce the paper's reported values -- red tape 0.761 vs 0.883, negative emotions 0.394 vs 0.880 -- so the deposit appears not to correspond to the reported analysis, which is a response-data observation, not an item-text one). The three items are instead a near-verbatim parallel of Hewlin's Facades of Conformity scale (item 22 vs Hewlin's "I suppress personal values that are different from those of the organization"), which the paper never cites. Extraction therefore follows Step 3b and describes what the live data actually is: instrument is the descriptive "Qiang et al. (2025) frontline retail staff survey, value-suppression block (questionnaire items 22-24)", not "Brotheridge & Lee Emotional Labour Scale". The table NAME and the dictionary Description ("Surface acting / value-suppression scale") should be corrected -- flagged for the orchestrator; no row was written to pending_index_notes.csv from this agent. (2) ENGLISH FALLBACK: administered in Chinese ("The survey instruments were first translated from English to Chinese using a forward-backward translation method"). No Chinese wording for items 22-24 exists in either place recoverability is scoped to: S1 File (the article's only Supporting Information file, sha256 a2b8f618be9d2de7bb31c113709bfe87ddd7dd682e5dc2816359a74d1444c343) carries English headers for every questionnaire item 17-42 except item 35 (a workplace-friendship item not in this table), and the article body prints no item text for this block. So the study's own English ships in the base fields with language=Chinese and no _translated columns (text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied). (3) MIDDLE ANCHORS UNLABELLED: the paper states only "All items were rated on a five-point Likert scale, with '1' to '5' representing five levels from 'strongly disagree' to 'strongly agree'", so option_text is populated at resp 1 and 5 and left blank at 2/3/4 rather than padded. instructions/section_prompt blank (no participant-facing instruction text is published); correct_response blank (no key). RIGHTS: no block, and the check was run in both directions. instrument_rights_register.csv has no row for Brotheridge & Lee's Emotional Labour Scale, for facades of conformity, or for Hewlin (54 rows searched on 'surface', 'emotional labo', 'brotheridge', 'facade', 'conformity', 'hewlin', 'deep acting'). Brotheridge & Lee's ELS rights are moot here because none of its wording is shipped -- the only ELS text in the record is the paper's one sample item, which is not in the CSV. For the wording that IS shipped, the originator question resolves to Hewlin's Facades of Conformity scale at most, and no restrictive clause from Hewlin is quotable: searches turned up no licence page, no fee, no permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution statement, only generic third-party boilerplate (a ProQuest 'reproduced with permission of the copyright owner' stamp on a journal PDF, and APA PsycTests's general permissions guidance) -- neither of which is a term stated by the rights holder about this instrument, per the PANAS precedent that a journal article's copyright notice is a notice about the article. Silence is permission (irw#1945 test), so extraction proceeded. The shipped words are in any case the study's own reworded English, published by the authors in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE Supporting Information file, not a verbatim reproduction of Hewlin's items. MAPPING (data_labels, Step 5b exempt, corroborated anyway): the S1 column HEADER is the item wording, and data/qiang_2025_red_tape.py maps the three full header strings to sa1/sa2/sa3 through a literal dict (SURFACE_ACTING) followed by df.rename + melt -- no enumerate, no column-index range, no row_number, so the derivation is 'code IS the source column name' with a mechanical rename and a shifted range is impossible. Corroborated against the data: live per-item mean/SD/n from item_stats.R are sa1 3.74/0.90/396, sa2 3.36/1.20/396, sa3 3.72/1.01/396, reproducing raw S1 columns 22, 23 and 24 (3.7449/0.9046, 3.3561/1.2021, 3.7172/1.0117, n=396 with zero missing) in that order; ceiling% 15.9/19.2/25.8 matches the raw 5-counts 63/76/102 of 396. The three profiles are mutually distinct, so no permutation of the texts reproduces the live table. TRANSCRIPTION DEVIATION: only the leading questionnaire numbering and Chinese enumeration comma ('22、'..'24、') were stripped; everything else is verbatim, including the curly apostrophe in "organization's" in sa2. DEPOSIT OBSERVATION (response data, not item text): S1 columns 47-50 (CO-1.1, C0-2.1, C0-3.1, CO) are an exact row-for-row duplicate of columns 17-20 (CO-1, C0-2, C0-3, CO-4), confirming the processing script's read of that 8-column block as a raw-file artifact; neither block is shipped by any IRW table. RETRY TEST: not applicable -- this is a clean pass, not a block.

note: Clean pass, 20 rows (4 items x 5 resp levels); validate_items.R --table-sets PASS on both the item set (fr1-fr4) and the resp set (1-5). Four caveats/findings. (1) THE CHINESE HEADER (S1 column 39, '35、我可以向同事倾诉心声') DOES NOT BELONG TO ANY SHIPPED ITEM. It is the only CJK header among the S1 File's 51 columns and it does sit inside the questionnaire's friendship block (items 33-37), but data/qiang_2025_red_tape.py's FRIENDSHIP dict ships only questionnaire items 33, 34, 36 and 37 as fr1-fr4 and drops column 39 entirely, so the live table contains no item for questionnaire number 35. The script's comment calls column 39 'item 35's Chinese-language duplicate of item 36'; that is WRONG on the data - the two columns agree on only 81 of 396 rows (r=0.21), have different distributions (item 35: 8/66/84/160/78 across resp 1-5, mean 3.5909; item 36: 7/28/74/199/88, mean 3.8409), and item 35 correlates far more strongly with items 33 (0.66) and 37 (0.61) than with 36 (0.21). They are two distinct administered items, one of which the authors simply never translated in the deposit's header row. So the Chinese header recovers no administered wording for fr1-fr4, and the English fallback applies to all four items exactly as it did for the batch_148 siblings - but on the ground that the Chinese item is not in this table, not on the ground that no Chinese exists anywhere. (2) ENGLISH FALLBACK: the study administered a Chinese questionnaire ('We translated the scales from English to Chinese and adapted the context to the participants' work settings'; 'The survey instruments were first translated from English to Chinese using a forward-backward translation method'). Recoverability is scoped to the deposit and the paper's own supplements: the article lists exactly ONE Supporting Information file (journal.pone.0327359.s001; no s002-s005 exist - the article HTML references only .s001), that file's header row is English for all four shipped items, and the article body prints no item text for this block and contains only one CJK token anywhere ('防控', in the Introduction). So the authors' own English ships in the base fields with language=Chinese and the _translated columns omitted (text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied). (3) INSTRUMENT NOT NAMED BY THE SOURCE: the string 'friendship' does not occur anywhere in the article. The Measures section names only the five analysed scales (Red Tape / Borst 2019, Negative Emotions / Watson 1988, surface and deep acting / Brotheridge & Lee 2002, customer orientation / Thomas et al. 2001), reports no alpha for this block, and cites no source scale for it. The label 'workplace friendship' is data/qiang_2025_red_tape.py's content-based description, so the instrument field names the questionnaire block rather than asserting an attribution (the items resemble the Nielsen/Jex/Adams and Riordan/Griffeth workplace-friendship prevalence tradition but reproduce neither verbatim). (4) MIDDLE ANCHORS UNLABELLED: the paper gives endpoints only - 'All items were rated on a five-point Likert scale, with "1" to "5" representing five levels from "strongly disagree" to "strongly agree."' - so option_text is populated at resp 1 and 5 and left blank at 2, 3 and 4 rather than padded. instructions and section_prompt are blank: no participant-facing instruction text is published in the article or its supplement. correct_response blank: no key, it is an agreement scale. MAPPING (data_labels, exempt from Step 5b): the S1 header string IS the item text, and the script maps each full header string to fr1-fr4 through a literal dict followed by df.rename + melt - no enumerate, no column-index range, no row_number - so the derivation is 'code IS the source column name' with a mechanical rename, and 4/4 codes are tied to the header they were renamed from. Corroborated against the data anyway: all 20 item x resp-level cells match the raw S1 columns exactly (fr1 7/68/74/178/69, fr2 6/85/42/165/98, fr3 7/28/74/199/88, fr4 2/105/72/117/100; n=396 each, zero missing, matching irw_table_sets' 1,584 rows), and the four count profiles are mutually distinct, so no permutation of the four texts reproduces the live table. RIGHTS: no block. itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv has no row for any workplace-friendship instrument (searched 'friend', 'workplace', 'trust', 'confid'; the only 'friend' hit is the De Jong Gierveld loneliness match strings, which none of these four items contain). The wording is published by the authors themselves in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE Supporting Information file, no external rights holder is identifiable, and no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause is quotable; silence is permission (irw#1945). No register row written. STEP 3b: matches - 4 live items on resp 1-5 with n=396 each, exactly S1 questionnaire items 33/34/36/37, and not one of the paper's five named scales. TRANSCRIPTION DEVIATIONS: the leading questionnaire numbering and Chinese enumeration comma ('33、'..'37、') was stripped from item_text; nothing else altered. The anchors are capitalised ('Strongly disagree'/'Strongly agree') where the paper prints them lowercase inside quotation marks, matching the four batch_148 sibling tables from this same source. DATA OBSERVATION (about the response table, not the item text): the four shipped items do not cohere as a scale - fr1-fr2 r=0.045 and fr3-fr4 r=-0.019 on the 396 complete raw rows, while the DROPPED item 35 correlates 0.66 and 0.61 with fr1 and fr4. The block would arguably be better represented with item 35 included (as a 5-item block) than without it; flagged for a human eye on the response data, not on the mapping, which carries no inference.
public_note: The 396 respondents were Chinese frontline retail staff answering a forward-back-translated Chinese questionnaire, but the study publishes no Chinese wording for these four items, so the item text shown here is the authors' own English from the S1 File column headers; the paper never names or analyses this block, so the instrument name given here describes the questionnaire block rather than reporting an attribution, and only the 1 and 5 endpoints of the five-point scale are labelled in the source. Item fr5 is questionnaire item 35, which the IRW processing script dropped as a presumed Chinese duplicate of item 36 until 2026-09-10; the response data shows they are different administered items (they agree on 81 of 396 rows, r = 0.208), so the item was restored and the response table rebuilt from 1584 to 1980 rows. It is coded fr5 rather than inserted in questionnaire order because fr1-fr4 were already published item codes. Item 35 is the one item in this block the deposit prints only in Chinese, so unlike the other four its English here was written by IRW, not by the study.
